# Grenat — reference for LLMs writing Grenat code

Grenat is a compiled language for AI agents: Ruby's syntax, static types (inferred inside bodies), effects checked by the compiler, and agents, prompts, tools and durable workflows built in. Files end in `.grn`. Read this whole page before writing code: Grenat is NOT Ruby, and code that looks like Ruby but ignores the rules below does not compile.

## Toolchain

```sh
grenat new --app desk        # an application: src/app.grn, src/config.grn, config/models.yml, tests/, db/migrations/
grenat check [file]          # type, effect and taint check: run it after every edit, fix every error
grenat test [file]           # offline tests (models, HTTP, shell, mail mocked)
grenat run file.grn args…    # runs `main`
grenat serve                 # routes, webhooks, schedules, job workers
grenat fmt                   # canonical layout
```

`grenat check` errors carry codes: E0100 unknown name, E0200 type, E0300 effect not granted, E0310 non-deterministic effect outside a workflow `step`, E0412 untrusted value reaching a sink, E0414 secret reaching a model, E0500 bad declaration. Fix the cause; never silence E0412 with `.trust!` unless the value is genuinely safe.

## Differences from Ruby (the rules that matter)

- Types are written on `def`/`tool`/`prompt` parameters and returns, and on struct fields; inferred everywhere else. `def total(items: Array(Item), rate: Float = 0.2) -> Float`.
- Types: `Int`, `Float`, `Bool`, `String`, `Money`, `Path`, `Email`, `Array(T)`, `Hash(K, V)`, `T?` (optional), `Result(T, E)`, `~T` (untrusted), `Secret`, `Attachment`.
- Optionals instead of nil everywhere: `user&.email || "unknown"`. Errors are values: `?` propagates a `Result`; `raise "msg"`, `raise ArgumentError, "msg"` and `begin … rescue KeyError, ArgumentError => e … end` also work (a `def` body may end with `rescue` without `begin`).
- No `method_missing`, `send`, `eval`, monkey-patching, `require "json"`, gems, `async`/`await`, `attr_accessor` (use a struct field or a `macro`). `require "./file"` only for your own files, at the top level.
- Construct a struct by calling its name: `Point(x: 1.0, y: 2.0)`; hash shorthand `{query:}`, keyword shorthand `f(to:, body:)`.
- One-line methods: `def norm = Math.sqrt(x * x + y * y)`. Class methods: `def self.load(...)`. Constants: `LIMIT = 10`, `API = "…"` inside a module (`GitHub::API`).
- Everything is concurrent without coloring: `xs.parallel_map(limit: 5) { |x| … }`, `race do … end`.
- Locals cannot be annotated (`x: Int = 1` does not parse); keywords (`until`, `end`, `in`…) cannot be parameter names; no `\` line continuation (break after an operator or a comma instead).
- Not in Grenat (don't use them): array set operators `&` / `|` (use `a.select { |x| b.include?(x) }`, `(a + b).uniq`), regular expressions (`/…/`, `=~`, `scan`, `match`), `strftime`, `freeze`, `step`, `each_char`, destructuring block parameters (`|(k, v), acc|`: take the pair, `pair[0]`), endless ranges outside an index (`(1..)`).
- Time: an instant is a `Float` (epoch seconds): `Time.now` (`uses time`), `Time.parse("2026-09-28T08:00:00+02:00")` (ISO 8601; a date alone is midnight UTC; invalid → `ArgumentError`), `Time.at(2026, 9, 28, 8, 0, 0)`; written in UTC by `Time.iso(t)` → `"2026-09-28T06:00:00Z"`, `Time.date(t)` → `"2026-09-28"`, `Time.weekday(t)` → 1 (Monday)…7 (cut to the millisecond, never rounded). `Time.today` is a `"YYYY-MM-DD"` string. `7.days`, `1.hour`, `2.min` are `Duration`s: `Time.now - 7.days` is a `Float`, `2.h - 30.min`, `3 * 1.h`, `1.h < 2.h`, `1.h == 3600` (a duration compares with its seconds), `d.to_i` (seconds). No time zones besides offsets, no `t.year` (use `Time.date`).

```ruby
struct Point
  x: Float
  y: Float

  def norm = Math.sqrt(x * x + y * y)
end

class Counter                    # a reference; @ivars need a type or a default
  @count: Int = 0

  def incr! = @count += 1
end

enum Shape
  Circle(radius: Float)
  Rect(w: Float, h: Float)
end

def area(s: Shape) -> Float
  case s
  in Circle(r) then 3.14159 * r * r
  in Rect(w, h) then w * h
  end
end

module Greeting
  def self.hello(name: String) -> String = "Hello, #{name}"
end
```

## Effects (capabilities)

A function that does I/O declares it with `uses`; a caller must cover its callees' effects, and `main` is the root. Missing one is E0300.

`llm` (calls a model) · `net("api.github.com")` (HTTP, SMTP or IMAP to that host; `Mail.connect("smtp://smtp.acme.io")` needs `net("smtp.acme.io")`; `net` alone = any host — use it when the host comes from configuration, e.g. `Mail.connect(Credentials.fetch(:smtp, :url))`: a host checked at run time must be granted) · `fs.read("./docs")`, `fs.write("out")` (path prefix) · `shell("git")` (that program) · `ssh("host")` · `db.read`, `db.write` (`db` = both) · `mcp("server")` · `env` (environment, credentials) · `human` (approval) · `time`, `random`.

```ruby
def main(args: Array(String)) uses llm, net("api.github.com"), env, fs.read("./docs")
  puts args.first
end
```

## Models and prompts

Models are configured in `config/models.yml` (the first is the default); keys come from `grenat credentials edit` (`openai: {api_key: …}`) or the provider's variable (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`…). Providers: anthropic, openai, gemini, mistral, xai, openrouter, groq, deepseek, together, ollama.

```yaml
fast:
  provider: anthropic
  name: claude-haiku-4-5
smart:
  provider: anthropic
  name: claude-opus-5
```

In a single file, declare them in code instead: `model :fast, provider: :anthropic, name: "claude-haiku-4-5"`.

A `prompt` is a function implemented by a model. Its return type becomes a JSON schema; the answer is validated and retried if malformed. `##` comments (on the prompt, on fields) are sent to the model as descriptions.

```ruby
enum Sentiment
  Positive
  Neutral
  Negative
end

struct Summary
  title: String         ## 8 words at most
  bullets: Array(String)  ## 3 to 5 key points
  sentiment: Sentiment
end

## Summarizes an article.
prompt summarize(article: String) -> ~Summary using :fast
  system "You are a concise analyst."
  user "Summarize:\n#{article}"
end
```

`user` also takes attachments: `user "Extract this invoice.", Pdf.read(path)` (`Image.read`, `Pdf.url`, `Image.url`).

## Untrusted values `~T` (taint)

Whatever comes from outside is untrusted: model answers, HTTP bodies, files read from the web, webhook payloads, shell output, MCP results, an agent's answer. (Inside a `tool`, its arguments are trusted: the tool is the trust boundary, so `approve! "Open #{title}?"` is allowed there.) You may read, print, or pass it to another prompt. It may NOT reach a sink — HTTP request, shell argument, file write, email, database write, HTML page, approval text — until cleaned (E0412):

```ruby
s = summarize(text)                                        # ~Summary
ok = s.check { |x| x.bullets.size.between?(3, 5) }?        # Summary, or the CheckError propagates
ok2 = s.check { |x| x.title.size > 0 }.or_else { s.approve(by: :human) }
fine = s.trust!                                            # explicit, grep-able: only when truly safe
```

`x.approve(by: :human)` shows the value to the human and returns it trusted, or raises `ApprovalDenied`; to review a model's text before printing it, use it (`reply.approve(by: :human)`) rather than putting the text in `approve!`. `x.check { … }` without `?` is a `Result`: `.or_else { … }` gives a fallback.

A field read from an untrusted value is untrusted too: `res.json["id"].check { |i| i > 0 }?`.

## Tools and agents

A `tool` is a function a model may call; its `##` doc and parameter types become the tool's description and schema. Tool arguments arrive validated: the tool is the trust boundary.

```ruby
## Reads a documentation page.
tool read_doc(path: String) -> String uses fs.read("./docs")
  File.read("./docs/#{path}")
end

## Opens a ticket in the tracker. Requires human approval.
tool open_ticket(title: String) -> Int uses net("tracker.acme.io"), human
  approve! "Open ticket “#{title}”?"
  Http.post("https://tracker.acme.io/tickets", json: {title:}).status
end
```

An `agent` is an actor with a mailbox. `run` is the built-in loop (model → tools → model…) that ends when the model produces the handler's return type, or when `budget`/`max_turns` runs out.

```ruby
struct Answer
  body: String            ## the reply, in the customer's language
  sources: Array(String)  ## pages used
end

agent Support
  model :smart
  tools read_doc, open_ticket
  budget usd: 0.50, time: 2.min
  max_turns 12
  instructions "Answer from the documentation only. Open a ticket for bugs."

  @handled: Int = 0

  on Ask(question: String) -> ~Answer
    @handled += 1
    run "Customer question: #{question}"
  end
end

def answer(question: String) -> String uses llm, fs.read("./docs"), net("tracker.acme.io"), human
  reply = spawn(Support).ask(Ask(question:))
  reply.check { |a| a.sources.any? }?.body
end
```

When a tool raises (including `approve!` denied, which raises `ApprovalDenied`), the error is sent back to the model as the tool's result and the loop goes on: that is how the model learns a denial. A tool is also an ordinary function: tests may call it directly. `run` raises `MaxTurnsExceeded` after `max_turns`, `BudgetExceeded` when the budget is spent.

`a.tell(Msg(...))` sends without waiting; `spawn_pool(Support, size: 4)` is a load-balanced pool; `within budget(usd: 1.00) do … rescue BudgetExceeded => e … end` caps spending; `tool_timeout 20` in an agent bounds each tool call. Agents can use MCP servers: `mcp :linear, url: "…", headers: {…}` then `tools mcp(:linear)`.

## Durable workflows, jobs, approvals

A `workflow` journals each `step`: after a crash or a human wait, finished steps are replayed, never re-billed. Inside a workflow, every `llm`/`net`/`time`/`random`/`human` effect must be inside a `step` (E0310).

```ruby
workflow publish(topic: String) uses llm, net("blog.acme.io"), human
  post = step(:draft) { summarize(topic).trust! }
  step(:review) { approve! "Publish “#{post.title}”?" }
  step(:publish) { Http.post("https://blog.acme.io/posts", json: {title: post.title}) }
end
```

A workflow run is identified by its name and arguments: calling it again with the same arguments (after a crash) replays the finished steps from the journal and runs the rest; pass a key such as the week's Monday (`weekly(monday: "2026-09-28")`) to get one run per period.

`enqueue(:publish, "rust")` (or `enqueue(:digest, in: 1.hour)`) queues a call for `grenat serve`'s workers; in a job, `approve!` waits for `Approvals.approve(id)` (also from `grenat console`).

## Standard library (most used)

- `Http.get/post/put/patch/delete(url, query:, headers:, json:, body:, timeout:)` → `status`, `ok?`, `headers`, `body`, `json` (body/headers/json untrusted).
- `Credentials.fetch(:github, :token)` → `Secret` (works in HTTP headers/URLs, `Db.connect`, `Mail.connect`, `Ssh.connect`; never printed, never sent to a model; a missing one raises `KeyError`). Use it for every token, password and connection URL: a spec's `GITHUB_TOKEN` becomes `Credentials.fetch(:github, :token)` (`github: {token: …}` in `grenat credentials edit`). `"Bearer #{token}"` is itself a `Secret`; comparing a secret to a string works (`assert_equal "Bearer t", header`). In tests without credentials, `Credentials.fetch(:a, :b)` is the stand-in secret `"test-a-b"`; `mock_credentials` sets others. `Env.fetch("NAME")`, `Env.fetch("NAME", "default")`, `Env.get("NAME")` (nil when unset), `Env.key?("NAME")` give plain strings (non-secret settings); in tests, `Env` sees only what `mock_env` gives (never the machine's environment).
- `File.read(path)`, `File.write(path, text)`, `File.lines(path)`, `Dir.list(dir)` (bare file names, not paths); `Json.parse(text)`, `Json.generate(v)`.
- `Shell.run(["git", "status"], timeout: 60, network: false)` → `status`, `ok?`, `stdout`, `stderr` (argument vector, never a shell line).
- `Mail.connect(url).send(from:, to: [...], subject:, body:)`.
- `Db.connect(url)` → `query(sql, [params], as: Row)`, `first`, `execute`, `transaction do … end`; `?` placeholders.
- Records: `database Env.fetch("DATABASE_URL")`, a struct with `table :tickets` and `id: Int?` gets `create`, `find`, `where`, `all`, `count`, `save`, `delete`, `with(field: v)`; `migration "001_x" do |db| db.migrate("CREATE TABLE …") end`, applied by `grenat migrate`.
- `embed(:docs, texts)` (an embedding model: `kind: embedding` in models.yml) + record field `embedding: Vector(1024)` + `Doc.nearest(:embedding, vector, limit: 4)`.
- `Conversation.load("chat.json", model: :fast, system: "…")` → `say(text)` (untrusted answer), `save(path)`.
- `xs.batch_map { |x| prompt_call(x) }`: batch API, half price, answers within 24 h.
- `transcribe(:whisper, Audio.read("call.mp3"))`, `Html.text(html)`, `Html.escape(s)`, `Ssh.connect("user@host", key: secret).run(["uptime"])`.
- Arrays/hashes/strings: Ruby's usual methods (`map`, `select`, `each_with_index`, `sort_by`, `take`, `join`, `split`, `include?`, `upcase`, `strip`, `to_i`, `to_f`, `to_s`, `size`, `first`, `any?`, `all?`, `partition`, `group_by`, `sum`, `flatten` / `flatten(depth)` (negative: all levels), `each_slice`, `each_cons`, `each_with_object`, `filter_map`, `tally`, `zip`, `min_by`, `minmax`, `uniq`, `sort { |a, b| b <=> a }`, `reduce(:+)`, `inject(0, :*)`, `inject(0) { … }`, `dig`, `transform_values`, `transform_keys`, `merge(h) { |k, a, b| … }`, `fetch(k, default)`, `delete_prefix`, `delete_suffix`, `start_with?`, `center`, `ljust`, `tr`, `squeeze`, `count("a-z", "^aeiou")` (several sets intersect), `gsub`/`sub` with strings, `then`…).
- Slices count characters, as in Ruby: `s[0, 4]`, `s[1..]`, `s[1..-2]`, `xs[2, 3]`, `xs[1...-1]` are `String?` / `Array(T)?` (`nil` when the start is past the end); they are read only (`xs[i] = v` assigns an item, `xs[0, 2] = v` and `s[0] = "x"` are errors: build a new value). `format("%.2f", x)`, `"%05d" % n`, `"%.3d" % n`, `"%s-%s" % [a, b]` format numbers as Ruby does (`%x` of a negative is `-ff`, not `..f01`); `x.round(2)` rounds.

## Serving: routes, webhooks, schedules

```ruby
get "/tickets/:id" do |req|
  id = req.params["id"].check { |i| i.to_i > 0 }?.to_i
  json({id:})
end

on_webhook "/github", secret: Credentials.fetch(:github, :webhook_secret), signature: :github do |req|
  event = req.json.check { |e| e["action"] == "opened" }?
  enqueue(:publish, "pull request")
  "ok"
end

every cron: "0 8 * * MON" do  # cron schedules are in UTC
  enqueue(:publish, "weekly digest")
end
```

A handler's value is the response: a string, a hash/record (JSON), `json(v)`, `html(page)` (escape untrusted with `Html.escape`), `status(201, v)`, `redirect(url)`, an integer status, `nil` (204). `stream do |out| … end` answers as Server-Sent Events; `expose "/mcp", tools: [:read_doc], agents: [Support], token: Credentials.fetch(:api, :token)` serves tools and agents over MCP.

Email in: `grenat serve` reads a mailbox (Gmail, Microsoft 365, any IMAP server) and hands each new message to its handler, then marks it seen (or moves it with `move_to:`); a handler that raises leaves it unseen, tried three times, then flagged.

```ruby
struct Triage
  urgent: Bool
  summary: String
end

prompt triage(subject: String, body: String, documents: Array(Attachment)) -> ~Triage using :fast
  user subject, body
  documents.each { |d| user d }  # attachments go to the model
end

on_email Credentials.fetch(:support, :imap_url), every: 1.minute, move_to: "Done" do |email|
  documents = email.attachments.select { |a| a.kind != "file" }  # PDFs, images, audio
  t = triage(email.subject, email.text, documents).check { |t| t.summary.size < 300 }?
  enqueue(:follow_up, t.summary) if t.urgent
end
```

The URL is `imaps://user%40acme.io:APP-PASSWORD@imap.gmail.com/INBOX` (folder in the path), a `Credentials` secret; `token: :fn` names a function returning an OAuth access token instead (Microsoft 365 requires one). `email` is an `IncomingEmail`: `from`, `from_name`, `to`, `cc` (`Array(String)`), `reply_to`, `subject`, `date` (`Float?`), `message_id`, `text`, `html`, `attachments` (`Array(Attachment)`: `kind` `document`/`image`/`audio`/`file`, `media_type`, `name`) — every field untrusted, the sender's address included. Reading the mailbox needs `net` (`net("imap.gmail.com")` for a literal URL).

## Tests

Tests run offline; every external call must be mocked. Put them in `tests/*_test.grn` (or `x_test.grn` with `require "./x"`).

```ruby
test "the agent answers from the docs" do
  mock :smart, replies: [
    call(:read_doc, path: "refunds.md"),                         # the model calls a tool…
    {body: "Refunds take 30 days.", sources: ["refunds.md"]},    # …then answers
  ]
  File.write("./docs/refunds.md", "Refunds: 30 days.")
  assert_equal "Refunds take 30 days.", answer("How long for a refund?")
end

test "a summary" do
  mock :fast, replies: [{title: "Rust 2.0", bullets: ["a", "b", "c"], sentiment: "Positive"}]
  assert_equal "Rust 2.0", summarize("…").trust!.title
end
```

Doubles: `mock :model, replies: [...]` (a reply is a value of the return type as a hash, a string, or `call(:tool, args…)`), `mock_http "GET https://api.x.com/*", json: {…}` (or `status:`, `body:`), `mock_shell "git status*", stdout: "…"`, `mock_mcp :linear, tools: {"create_issue" => "L-1"}`, `mock_embed :docs`, `mock_credentials({"github" => {"token" => "t"}})`, `mock_env({"SMTP_URL" => "smtp://smtp.test"})` (what `Env` reads in this test), `mock_mail(raise: "SMTP down")` (sends raise `MailError`; `raise: nil` restores), `with_human(approve_all) do … end` (or `deny_all`), `freeze_time("2026-09-28T08:00:00Z") do … end` (`Time.now`/`Time.today` answer that instant inside; only in a `test` block), `request :get, "/tickets/1"`, `deliver_webhook "/github", json: {…}`, `deliver_email(from: "ada@example.com", subject: "Refund", text: "…", attachments: [Pdf.read("invoice.pdf")])` (runs the `on_email` handler; returns `{"status" => "seen"}`, `"moved"` with `"folder"`, or `"failed"` with `"error"`), `Jobs.perform`, `Mail.deliveries`, `Http.requests`. `freeze_time`, `mock_env`, `mock_mail`, `deliver_email` and `Http.requests` work only inside a `test` block. Assertions: `assert x`, `assert_equal expected, actual`, `assert_raises TaintError { … }`.

- `mock :model, replies: [...]` fails the test ("mock has no reply left") when the model is called more often than replies were given: that is how a test proves a workflow did not call the model again.
- `mock_http` options: `json:`, `body:`, `status:`, `headers:` (the response's); an unstubbed request raises `HttpError`. `Http.requests` lists what the test sent (stubbed or not), in order, as hashes: `req = Http.requests.last; assert_equal "POST", req["method"]; assert_equal({"title" => "x"}, req["json"]); assert_equal "Bearer t", req["headers"]["Authorization"]` (also `"url"`, `"body"`; `"json"` is nil when the body is not JSON; a secret stays a `Secret`, equal to its text).
- `Mail.deliveries` is an array of hashes with string keys: `m["from"]`, `m["to"]` (an array), `m["subject"]`, `m["body"]`.
- To simulate a crash between two workflow steps, make the later step fail (`mock_mail(raise: "SMTP down")` before a sending step), assert the error, undo it (`mock_mail(raise: nil)`), then run the workflow again with the same arguments: finished steps replay from the journal.
- Error classes: `TaintError`, `CapabilityError`, `SecretError`, `CheckError`, `ApprovalDenied`, `BudgetExceeded`, `MaxTurnsExceeded`, `TimeoutError`, `HttpError`, `MailError`, `KeyError`, `ArgumentError`, `TypeError`, `LlmError`, `RuntimeError` (a bare `raise "msg"`). `rescue` names the class.
- The stand-in secret `"test-a-b"` is not a URL: a test that sends mail or connects to a database gives a real-looking one, `mock_credentials({"smtp" => {"url" => "smtp://u:p@smtp.acme.io:587"}, "github" => {"token" => "t"}})` (it replaces all the stand-ins).
- Mocked models cost nothing, so a dollar budget cannot be exceeded in a test; test `max_turns` instead (give more tool-call replies than turns).
- `GRENAT_LOG=1 grenat test …` prints each model, tool and HTTP call.

## Checklist before answering

1. Every function doing I/O has `uses …`, and `main` covers everything.
2. Every value from a model, HTTP, a webhook or a tool's output is `check`ed (or `approve`d) before reaching a sink.
3. Secrets come from `Credentials.fetch` and never go into a prompt.
4. Prompts and handlers return typed structs with `##` field docs.
5. `grenat check` passes, then `grenat test`.
